The advocacy workflow

One build becomes a campaign you can actually ship: a base post, six archetype takes, twelve social posts, a drip per shipped piece, and a video, tracked as seven flat Asana tasks that the files tick. Written to be read cold.

What it is for

You finish a project. This plugin turns it into content with no task-management layer on top. advocacy-intake promotes the repo and creates the seven tasks. advocacy-cycle writes every piece from the build ledger and ticks the board from what is live. last-looks checks everything before it leaves. Behind them: x-article for the long-form X piece and its post series, script-to-video for a placeholder video to re-record against, and the voice passes (personal-style, corporate-style, de-slop) every draft goes through.

It needs project-workflow installed first. That plugin owns the repo's .hub/, the Asana project, and the ledger. This one never creates any of them.

Before you start

/plugin marketplace add samgutentag-deepgram/project-workflow
/plugin install project-workflow@project-workflow
/plugin marketplace add samgutentag-deepgram/advocacy-workflow
/plugin install advocacy-workflow@advocacy-workflow

Start a new Claude Code session afterward, and check the Asana connector can answer "list my Asana workspaces". The first advocacy command reads ~/.claude/advocacy-workflow.yml and interviews you for anything missing (config.py --missing shows what). Video rendering also needs uv, ffmpeg, and DEEPGRAM_API_KEY.

The lab convention

Work happens in a private repo named thing-lab under lab_root. If it ships, it is snapshotted once into a public repo named thing, with .hub/ and advocacy/ stripped from every commit. -lab is private, the bare name is public, and nothing ever flows back from the public twin.

The seven tasks

Every promoted campaign gets one Asana project with the same seven flat tasks, no sections, no subtasks, in this order:

  1. Public repo
  2. Personal blog live
  3. Corporate blog live
  4. X Article live
  5. Drip written and scheduled
  6. Video live
  7. 90 day review (the only one with a due date: day 0 plus 90)

Ticking a task is both the approval and the record. You tick by hand, or /advocacy-cycle sync ticks from the files: public_repo in hub.yml, a published: URL in a content file, a drip with six written posts, a dated review entry in the ledger. No script ever unticks, and there is never an eighth task. An exploration, a project with no day 0, has zero tasks.

The happy path

  1. Build. mkdir ~/LABS/thing-lab && cd $_ && git init. Commit as you go.
  2. Make the hub. /project-hub init creates .hub/ and the Asana project. Log friction and decisions with /project-hub capture as they happen; the ledger cannot be backfilled.
  3. Promote. /advocacy-intake reads the repo cold, writes advocacy/advocacy.md with one falsifiable claim and the reader, sets day 0, and creates the seven tasks.
  4. Flip. Rewrite history into build order, strip .hub/ and advocacy/ from every commit, push thing public, then record it as public_repo: in .hub/hub.yml. That line ticks Public repo.
  5. Start the cycle. /advocacy-cycle init writes advocacy/notes.md from the ledger, every fact cited, and scaffolds the three content files.
  6. Draft. /advocacy-cycle draft blog-base, then /advocacy-cycle draft takes, then /advocacy-cycle draft social. Each file arrives as beats, HTML comments that scaffold one section with its word budget and allowed facts. Write into them, then delete them. The company blog is the same text with voice_corporate applied, not a second draft.
  7. Check. /last-looks advocacy/content/blog-base.md advocacy/content/social.md runs de-slop and your voice pass, then every mechanical check, one finding per line. Nothing is ship-ready while a finding is open.
  8. X Article. /x-article turns the approved base post into x-article.md, its paste page and 5:2 cover, the blog mirror, and a 10 to 15 post series. Approved means status: approved or a published: URL in the base's frontmatter.
  9. Ship. Publish by hand, then /advocacy-cycle ship advocacy/content/blog-base.md <url>. It records the URL under published: and syncs the file from the live page, never the reverse. The public video URL ships onto content/video-script.md the same way; /advocacy-cycle render makes the placeholder you re-record against.
  10. Drip. /advocacy-cycle drip <piece-url> --type blog writes six dated posts, one per archetype, Tuesdays and Thursdays, skipping launch_blackouts. Write them from notes.md, then /last-looks the file.
  11. Post. As each goes live: /advocacy-cycle post <drip-file> <n> <permalink>. It writes the permalink on that post and appends to content/published.log.
  12. Sync. /advocacy-cycle sync ticks every task the files prove complete and prints the evidence. Run it any time; /advocacy-cycle alone prints status.
  13. Review. On or after day 90, /project-hub capture a ledger entry titled 90 day review: did the claim hold. Then sync ticks the last task.

The six archetypes

Everything written for a reader fans out across six developer archetypes, always in this order: one section each in the takes, the social pool, and every drip.

ArchetypeWho they are
Curious devHas never heard of this. Wants the wow moment in one breath, no jargon.
ExplorerPoking at the space. Wants the measured number, how it was measured, and its edges.
BuilderWants to build it too. The copyable pattern, started inside a minute.
ScalerRuns this at volume. Cost, latency under load, spend controls, where it breaks.
ChampionCarrying this into their team. The argument they can forward as is.
Partner devOn an adjacent platform. Where this touches their stack and what their users gain.

Where every file ends up

advocacy/
  advocacy.md                   the frozen claim and the reader. intake writes it once
  notes.md                      every fact, cited. the only source content may use
  notes.companion.md            what each fact means and where it came from
  content/
    blog-base.md                the base post
    archetype-takes.md          six pickup briefs, one per archetype
    social.md                   six X posts and six LinkedIn posts, one pair per archetype
    x-article.md                the X Article text, with x-article-paste.html and x-cover-5x2.png
    x-series.md                 the 10 to 15 post series for the Article
    video-script.md             the script render reads, when there is a video
    drips/<date>-<slug>.md      six dated posts for one shipped piece
    published.log               one line per drip post that went live
  renders/                      base-layer videos. gitignored
  assets/                       figures you authored

Settings

All in ~/.claude/advocacy-workflow.yml: one person, one machine, every campaign. The interview fills the first four; the rest are added when a skill asks for them.

KeyWhat it is
asana_workspaceYour Asana workspace gid. The one fact the interview has to ask.
lab_rootWhere lab repos live. Default ~/LABS.
voice_personalThe skill writing in your voice. Default personal-style; name someone else's to ghostwrite.
voice_corporateThe company voice skill. Default corporate-style.
x_handleThe handle that posts the X Article and the series.
person_slugThe person credited in every utm_content, as first_last.
blog_base_urlYour personal blog. Its host is how sync tells a personal URL from a corporate one.
blog_utm_sourceThe one utm_source allowed to carry the person, used on the blog mirror.
utm_domainsThe owned domains that get UTM tags, comma separated. Also the corporate blog hosts for sync.
launch_blackoutsDates no drip or series post may land on, comma separated.
console_signup_urlWhere every video's closing call to action points. Defaults to the Deepgram console signup.

Rules that never bend

  • Facts come only from notes.md. No entry, no claim.
  • No number without a source. Every number of two or more digits is a literal token in notes.md; a wrong one is fixed there first.
  • Nothing is done without a permalink. A task ticks on a published: URL or a posted permalink, never because a draft exists.
  • Never write to .hub/. That is project-hub's.
  • Never edit advocacy.md. The claim is frozen. If a draft contradicts it, the draft is wrong or the campaign is over.

Status, 2026-10-01. Describes version 0.4.0. Every command, path, and setting was read from the skills and scripts.
